overview: This file combines U.S. diplomatic correspondence and naval intelligence on Japanese ship movements from 1940 to 1943. Its central thread is the Asaka Maru’s voyage to Europe: a dispute over armed guards during its Panama Canal transit, questions about German cargo and British contraband controls, and a changed return route. Other reports track Japanese warships, transports, aircraft, and submarines across Asia and beyond.
interest: The Asaka correspondence connects canal security, neutral-vessel law, British blockade policy, and Japanese-German naval exchange.
